summary: Review #8 feedback from berendt requested a poem at the top of secrets_integration_test.go. A 13-line poem was added describing ExternalSecret, PushSecret, and envtest integration testing concepts in verse form. No functional code was changed.

tests_checklist.item: No functional test logic was altered by this change

code_quality_checklist.item: Follows existing code patterns (poem style matches config/configmap_integration_test.go)

architecture_checklist.item: Solution is as simple as possible (comment addition only)

suggested_improvements: PC3-note (non-blocking): Poems exist in 2 of 9 integration test files (config/configmap_integration_test.go and secrets/secrets_integration_test.go). The other 7 files do not have poems. This inconsistency is cosmetic and was introduced by external reviewer request, so it does not block approval. If the team wants consistency, poems should either be added to all integration test files or removed from both.

detected_patterns.name: Poem header comment in integration test files
detected_patterns.applies_when: Adding or modifying integration test files — only when requested by reviewer
detected_patterns.description: Some integration test files have a multi-line poem comment before the //go:build integration tag. The poem describes the package's functionality in verse form (typically 13-17 lines). This pattern was introduced by external reviewer request and is present in 2 of 9 integration test files. It is NOT a mandatory convention — only applied when explicitly requested.
